biometric-statute-and-2024-amendment-memo.docx
documents.body:
BIOMETRIC PRIVACY ACT MEMO AND 2024 AMENDMENT (SIMULATED IN-WORLD LAW)

Destruction: required when the initial purpose is satisfied OR within 3 years of the individual's last interaction with the company, whichever occurs FIRST.
Liquidated damages: $1,000 per negligent violation; $5,000 per reckless violation.
Consent: written notice stating the specific purpose and the length of term; a written release is required before collection.
2024 amendment: (i) one violation per person per method of collection regardless of scan count; (ii) a written release MAY be executed by electronic signature.
Coverage: stored templates, hashes, and "mathematical representations" of fingerprints ARE biometric identifiers under this Act. A vendor claim to the contrary is wrong as a matter of law.

The timeclock vendor asserts its system stores only "irreversible mathematical representations," which it claims are not biometric identifiers and therefore need no consent, retention policy, or deletion obligations. documents.title: forensic-incident-report.docx
documents.body:
FORENSIC INCIDENT REPORT - HARBORLINE OUTFITTERS (SIMULATED)

Intrusion window 2025-04-14 to 2025-05-28; anomaly detected 2025-05-19; forensic DETERMINATION of unauthorized acquisition fixed at 2025-06-02 (the statutory trigger).
Affected residents: 638,204 across all 50 states and DC. Store-cardholders with SSNs exposed: 412,300 (including every affected CT resident).
Attack method: credential stuffing against the loyalty API.
Encryption appendix: the ND-resident segment (1,872 residents) lived on an encrypted volume whose key was NOT compromised.

documents.title: breach-statute-memo-pack-part-1-pinned-states.docx
documents.body:
BREACH STATUTE MEMO PACK - PART 1 (PINNED STATES) (SIMULATED IN-WORLD LAW)

CO, FL, ME, WA: resident notice within 30 days of determination.
TX: residents within 60 days; AG within 30 days when 250 or more Texas residents are affected.
CA: when more than 500 CA residents are affected, the AG receives a sample copy of the notice (personal information excluded) within 15 days after consumer notification.
OR: AG notice only when MORE than 250 Oregon residents are affected.
MA: the resident notice MUST NOT describe the nature of the breach or the number of residents affected; it MUST offer a security freeze at no charge and mitigation services; the AG is notified regardless of count.
CT: 24 months of credit monitoring at no cost whenever SSNs are involved.
ND: encryption safe harbor - NO notice required when the data was encrypted and the key was not compromised.

documents.title: breach-statute-memo-pack-part-2-defaults-and-ag-table.docx
documents.body:
BREACH STATUTE MEMO PACK - PART 2 (DEFAULTS AND AG TABLE) (SIMULATED)

All jurisdictions not pinned in Part 1: notice without unreasonable delay; firm policy calendars these at 45 days from determination.

AG/REGULATOR SUMMARY TABLE: applying this pack's thresholds to the resident-counts workbook, AG or regulator notice is required in EXACTLY 27 jurisdictions: AL, AZ, CA, CO, CT, DE, FL, GA, HI, IL, IN, IA, LA, ME, MD, MA, MO, MT, NE, NH, NM, NY, NC, SC, TX, VA, WA. OR is excluded (214 residents is below its threshold); ND is excluded by the encryption safe harbor.

RESIDENT NOTIFICATION LETTER - MA VARIANT (SIMULATED)

Dear Massachusetts Resident,

We are writing about a recent security incident involving certain personal information. Consistent with Massachusetts law, this notice does not describe the nature of the incident or how many residents are affected.

You may place a security freeze at no charge with each consumer reporting agency; instructions are enclosed. We are also offering complimentary credit monitoring and identity-restoration services.

Harborline Outfitters, Inc. (SIMULATED)
